title: Answering While Cut Off — Four Mercenaries Who Must Agree
description: The CAP theorem after Brewer and Gilbert and Lynch: four mercenaries and their ravens, and why a cut-off tent cannot both answer at once and answer as the others would.
question: When one part of a system is cut off from the rest, should it keep answering and risk being wrong, or stay silent until it can be sure? Can it ever have both?
how: We find out by exploring what four mercenaries at the foot of Mount Phyle could promise when hunting hawks cut one tent off from the others.

papers.title: Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services
